_doc: Curated map of well-known off-chain tickers → their canonical XRPL issuers (if any). Read by token_naming.resolve_display(). When a decoded currency name matches one of these keys but the issuer is NOT in canonical_issuers, /token, /whales, /check etc. render the collision-qualified form (e.g. 'USDT (usdxrp.net — not Tether)'). canonical_issuers=[] means NO canonical XRPL issuer exists — every match is a collision. Add cautiously; a new entry retroactively re-qualifies every existing display.
_source_of_truth: Ripple's RLUSD launch announcement (2024); public issuer registries at xrpscan.com and xrplf.org/registry (spot-checked 2026-09-06). Update this file, not code, when a legitimate issuer changes hands.
_bridges_doc: Bridge/wrapped-asset issuers that legitimately mint XRPL-side representations of off-chain tokens. When a token's issuer is in a bridge's issuers list AND its decoded ticker is in that bridge's tickers list, resolve_display() treats it as canonical (no collision label) with category = wrapped_bridge. This overrides the collision path — a WBTC issued by an Axelar/Midas bridge is the bridged form, not a collision claim against mainstream WBTC. Added 2026-09-08 after row #4 (SOL from rfmS3zqr...) surfaced in the curator queue as a false-positive collision.

midas_xrpl.name: Midas / Axelar bridge — XRPL wrapped assets
midas_xrpl.citation: curator-verified 2026-09-08 (Charlie ruling). Existing token_category_history entries for this issuer at wrapped_bridge tier since 2026-09-06 seed cover 8 of these tickers (SOIL, USDC.axl, USDf, WBTC, WETH, mBTC, mTBILL, mXRP); SOL + SHX added by this bridges section to keep the collision-check code aligned with the curator seed.
midas_xrpl.note: Bridge-issued XRPL representations of off-chain assets. Ticker match here is the bridged form, not a collision — do NOT set ticker_collision=TRUE for these (issuer, ticker) pairs.

_gateways_doc: Custodial fiat/BTC/ETH gateway issuers on XRPL — same collision-override semantics as bridges section (bridge-issued tickers → canonical, not collision), but distinct category (stablecoin_gateway) for editorial clarity. Populated conservatively as of 2026-09-08 — only issuers with strong evidence (matching domain + long-standing public address) are whitelisted here. Two-way toml proof walker has not yet run against these issuers as of add-date (domain_two_way_proof='unchecked'), so citations lean on domain match + historical public knowledge. Any addition here should specify: issuer address(es), tickers they issue, citation URL to the issuer's own published address page (or their xrp-ledger.toml).

bitstamp.name: Bitstamp — historic XRPL fiat/crypto gateway
bitstamp.citation: AccountRoot Domain field = 'bitstamp.net' (issuer_facts snapshot 2026-09-08); long-standing public address (see https://xrpscan.com/account/rvYAfWj5gh67oV6fW32ZzP3Aw4Eubs59B). Bitstamp deprecated new XRPL-side issuance around 2018 but the outstanding tokens remain tradeable; USD IOU shows 10,962 trades in trailing 30d, BTC shows 5,487 — clearly still-in-use custodial-gateway rails. Two-way toml proof pending — add when the walker runs against this issuer.
bitstamp.note: Historic gateway. USD + EUR are fiat-backed custodial rails; BTC + ETH are the gateway's issuance of those tickers (not native, not collisions in the impostor sense).
